summary: All ten records checked. II mqadašle is the consecration event; mqadše/mqadašto denote a sacred state or attributive status. The latter need not assert a particular prior event.
Existing 12/9 includes both finite mqadašle and attributive mqadše; form presence within a Preterit quotation does not make its secondary adjective finite.
The prayer token nəzqadaš has Syriac morphology and occurs in quoted liturgical language. Its supplied odd translation is not repaired or used to populate a Turoyo box.
New II Infectum and Infectum-wa attest the inherited consecration meaning with church, candles and Eucharistic offering. These are ritual participants, not separate numbered senses.
Detransitive kmiqadəš with an explicit human undergoer at 2.31/4859 confirms a finite process distinct from the already filled Part. Pass. sacred-state cell. Round-1 Detransitive sense 1 is reused.
The patriarch’s Ḥnan ... hoḏe ʕito ḥaḏto line is quoted literary Syriac; the adjacent Xori Brahim version is the Turoyo evidence. Form convergence does not make both independent native attestations.
Suffix spellings and agreement are preserved, including Mqadašše, mqadšole and feminine mqadašto with ḥubo. No existing text or inherited gloss is rewritten.
Verify the wording and language of PrS 72/39 nəzqadaš ma ḥṭiṯe. Does it intentionally misquote the prayer, and should quoted Syriac appear only in a note rather than native paradigm boxes?
How far is mqadše lexicalised as holy, particularly for sacred books and entrusted property? The present revision keeps the inherited grouping and does not multiply senses.
Jan 3.21/488: is unprefixed mqadšalle a contracted Preterit or Infectum? The English generalization does not settle the form, so it is not selected.
Jan 2.31/4858: identify the subject of feminine kəmqadšo and the undergoer of the following kmiqadəš. The clearer human-subject verse 4859 supplies the Detransitive example.
Jan 4.II/1044: confirm agreement and lexical sacred status of mqadašto with ḥubo; preserve the source wording.
Jan 3.44/1235: what is the antecedent of -le in komqadšile, the bread/body or the whole offering?
Correct the adjective ending in eines grünen Baumes.
rationale: After genitive eines the adjective requires -en. The edition repeats the erroneous ending, but the German inflection is unambiguous.

summary: Sacred status applies to books, places and church vessels as well as water and entrusted property. Attributive and predicative uses do not each require a new sense.

The round-1 Detransitive sacred-state sense extends to a firstborn consecrated to God and to love of homeland described as sacred. The homeland clause is an evaluative use, not evidence of a consecrating event.
